summary: Quiet research week: one new study (shorting rallies into falling EMAs: no edge) plus the Nov 7 supply-breaks study, whose long side is the best new lead (buy the hold after a stock clears big overhead supply, only in top-20% groups: +0.48R, t 2.3, both halves). Nothing passed the promotion rule and none of last week's plan was built, so the 11-year re-test is still the top job. Live warning: the Oct 15 shallow-thrust high-beta list finished -20% vs the market +0.7%, and the Nov 4 one is -6% after 7 days, yet the playbook still says 'Press, size up' after every thrust. Best next step: re-test the core edges on 11 years (#1) and split the playbook's post-thrust state into deep vs shallow (#2).

items.title: Re-test the core edges on 11 years of history (warehouse step 2), then the stacked R
items.where: tools/warehouse (11-year Yahoo data on branch warehouse-data); later a stack line on launchPicksCard and lineupCard
items.how: Carried over from last week, not started. Almost every edge we use was found on ~2 bull-heavy years with 2 deep thrusts. Put the lined-up dip trade and the supply-break hold into the 11-year warehouse with fixed columns: post-thrust window (deep vs shallow), leading group (top 20-30%), lifecycle BUY, SPY above 50-day, breadth state, extension at the leg high. Only lifts that survive go into a stacked expected R on each live trade.
items.test: Pre-register the columns (grade 85%+ before outcomes). Each lift = R with minus without, per date, clustered by month, t 2+, same sign in both halves AND pre-2024 vs 2024+. Stacked R scored on the later half only: top fifth minus bottom fifth 0 and rank IC 0.05+.
items.kill: Post-thrust or leading-group lift about 0 before 2024: those edges are a 2-year artefact, drop them from grades and say so on the cards. Stacked R with IC under 0.05: show proven single tags only.

items.title: Post-thrust playbook: split deep vs shallow thrusts before saying 'Press'
items.where: playbook_state (playbook.py state 'thrust' advice and setup verdicts); washout_thrust card
items.how: The playbook treats every thrust the same and today says 'Press, size up'. But the washout scorecard says shallow thrusts are different: Oct 15 (SPY only -2% off high) high-beta list -20.1% vs all stocks +0.7%; Nov 4 (-3.5%) -6.1% vs -1.4% after 7 sessions; deep thrusts (Apr 2025, Mar 2026) +26% / +34%. Turn-leaders says post-thrust breakouts still beat ordinary ones after shallow thrusts (+1.7% vs +4.1% deep), so the fix may be 'select, don't size up' rather than 'avoid'. Split the state into post-thrust deep / shallow and re-score each setup's verdict in each.
items.test: Existing trade backtest (trade_bt by state) re-cut by thrust depth (deep = SPY 8%+ pullback and T2108 25 or under), per thrust clustered, both halves; then confirm on the 11-year warehouse where there are far more thrusts. Build if shallow post-thrust R is below deep by t 2+ in both halves.
items.kill: Shallow post-thrust R about equal to deep (within 0.1R) or halves disagree: keep one post-thrust state.

items.title: Supply breaks: a 'held the break' card for top-group stocks, plus the real-fail exit
items.where: new info-only layer 'supply_breaks' (Setups tab card + forward ledger); 'real fail' as an exit tag on Launch picks, lined-up buys and box longs
items.how: Live list of stocks that closed above big overhead supply in the last ~15 sessions: phase (retesting / working off / cleared / real fail), sessions vs the 13-session clock, group percentile. Grade: top-20% group = buy the hold above the line (next open, stop 0.5 ADR under the level); bottom-half group = skip. Separately flag 'real fail' (3 closes under the level AND 1 ADR below) on open longs, since those lagged -9.2% vs +8.6% at 21 days. Information only, logged forward like the lined-up ledger.
items.test: Already: top-20% groups +0.48R (t 2.3, n 509, 278 dates, both halves), +3.2% vs matched breakouts at 21d (t 4.3). Not proven yet because windows overlap and group ranks use today's lists. Confirm on the 11-year warehouse with point-in-time groups (item 1), plus 20+ live dates in the forward ledger.
items.kill: Top-group lift under t 2 on 11 years, or live ledger average R below 0 after 30 closed trades. The short side is already dead (-0.08R, no cut positive in both halves).

items.title: Launch picks: one open pick per sub-theme across weeks
items.how: Got worse this week: this Friday's #1 is ACN, the 4th IT Services pick in 4 weeks (IT stopped -17%, CTSH -2.5%, CDW +8.8%), plus 2 Enterprise SaaS (ASAN -12%, TEAM -3%). The 9 entered picks average -2.9% vs SPY so far (early in 13-week holds, so not a verdict). Proposal: skip a sub-theme that already has an open Launch pick (or cap at 2) and take the next name.
items.test: launch.replay both ways on every past week: 13-week result vs SPY, worst open-book drawdown, t in both halves. Build only if the average is the same or better (within 1 pt) and the worst open-book drawdown is smaller.
items.kill: Average drops more than 1 pt vs SPY or a half turns negative: keep the current rule (concentration in the leading group may be the edge).

items.title: Lined-up buys: half the stops hit on entry day; check the fill and stop rule
items.how: Better than last week but not yet good: 39 filled, 15 stopped at -1R, 24 open marked +13R in total, so about -0.05R a trade vs the +0.84R backtest. 7 of the 15 stops hit the same day as entry (VTRS, PTC, BILL, TRV, CDW, AVTR, CNC) and 3 more the next day. Risk is ~1 ADR (stop = dip-day low), so an entry at the dip-day-high break can be stopped by one normal day. Check the backtest's same-day-stop rate against the live one; if live is much higher, the live fill (max of open, trigger) or the intraday stop check differs from the backtest.
items.test: Backtest same-day stop rate vs live (now 7 of 39 = 18%); after 30 closed trades: average R vs +0.84R, split by gate state and by stage (Blossom vs Quiet build).
items.kill: 30 closed trades with average R below 0 while the gate said buy: card switches to 'hold off' until item 1 is done.

items.title: Agent layers: forward log still too thin; the macro brief's risk field never varies
items.how: 360 settled ideas but only 16 dates (rule needs 20+). Closest: macro_tailwind t 1.99, both halves positive, but only 27 'bad' ideas over 8 dates; the code-only macro-fit backtest says no edge (t -0.03 on 6,757 signals), so treat it as likely noise. The macro brief said 'high' risk on 269 of 269 settled ideas, so brief_low_risk can never be tested; the brief needs a relative scale (vs its own last 20 days) to be measurable. That is an agent prompt change, Adam's call.
items.test: t 2+ over 20+ dates, same sign both halves.
items.kill: No agent layer at |t| 1+ after ~100 more settled ideas: cut the catalyst agent to earnings-date checks only (saves ~20-40 searches a weekday). Macro brief risk still constant after the change: drop the risk field from the log.
